velocity.basis: Measured first-party at 3ad6a2e46 over the last 14 days of non-merge commits touching *.go (added+deleted): 137, 220, 351, 503, 506, 557, 661, 709, 1013, 1286, 1696. Band 137-1696, median ~561 lines changed per commit. All six milestones (400/210/300/330/420/140) sit inside that band. 1800 LOC over 3.0 days = 600/day, inside the observed band (a single recent commit was 1286). The doc's own estimate is 2-3 days; this plan lands at 3.0, the TOP of the box, and says so rather than compressing to fit.

measurement_posture.platform_of_record: darwin/arm64, go1.26.6, macOS 26.5.2 (25F84) - planner-verified P1. Every number in the report is a darwin/arm64 number.
measurement_posture.gpu: NONE. The spike is pure Go CPU + heap work: no model load, no ollama call, no GPU. It does NOT take rig.lock and MUST NOT take it - rig.lock is a GPU MUTEX ONLY (tools/launchd/rig-lock.sh:16, tools/launchd/mission-control.sh:15, .claude/skills/mission-control/SKILL.md:445). Holding it for a ~1h CPU sweep would needlessly block GPU eval consumers. A later executor must not infer a lock requirement from the phrase 'runs on the rig'.
measurement_posture.rig_quietness: OBSERVED, NEVER ACQUIRED. `ls "$HOME/.ailang/state/rig.lock.d"` is run immediately BEFORE and AFTER the full matrix run and both lines are pasted into the report header. A concurrent GPU eval contends for memory bandwidth and cores; the five-trial median + ordinal pairing + tie/spread rerun is the doc's designed defence, and ordinal pairing means contention hits candidate and control alike.
measurement_posture.budget: WALL-CLOCK, not GPU-hours. 76 measured points x 5 trials = 380 fresh-process invocations per full pass (plus B-LEN's 40, plus reruns). Estimated ~30-90 minutes at -benchtime=1s; the executor records ACTUAL elapsed wall-clock in the report.
measurement_posture.peak_rss_ceiling: 4 GB. B1's heaviest cell (C0, m=4096, L=16384) retains ~1.07 GB PER ITERATION (4096 results x 16385 elements x 16 B interface headers) and the benchmark design mandates keeping them live. Release the result slice at the end of each b.N iteration; runner records /usr/bin/time -l max RSS per invocation; a cell breaching 4 GB is pinned to -benchtime=1x with the deviation and reason recorded in its command string. The rig has a documented history of eval-driven OOM kernel panics.

doc_ac_ambiguities.AMB_1_cell_granularity: AC-1 (doc:320-322) never defines 'cell' at grid granularity: row x arm = 32, grid point x arm = 76. RESOLVED to the strict 76 reading. The cheap reading would let a passing report omit 44 measured points.
doc_ac_ambiguities.AMB_2_clause_d_has_no_matrix_row: GENUINE DOC GAP. doc_ac_ambiguities.AMB_3_no_verdict_for_an_invalid_instrume: AC-2 (doc:323-325) reds if the C0 control fails to reach L-ratio >= 8 ('instrument can't see a positive -> B1 is invalid'), but AC-5 (doc:336-339) admits ONLY GO or STOP and forbids hedging. The plan references them by pointer and never paraphrases them into a gate.
hard_constraints.primary_descope_lever: DOC-SANCTIONED ONLY: if C2's lock-free O(K) shared-chunk prepend cannot be landed in budget, mark C2's columns infeasible with the reason recorded and proceed - the kill criterion tolerates it if C1 passes (doc:419). Removes ~0.4 day and 32 of the 76 measured points. A GO still requires ONE candidate to pass ALL FIVE clauses.
hard_constraints.no_production_wiring: ZERO changes under internal/, cmd/, std/, examples/. No parser/typechecker/codegen surface, no syntax, no semantics, no .ail files. The spike IMPORTS internal/eval read-only; importing is not modifying.
hard_constraints.out_of_scope_lc2: The production accessor layer/seam and the listrep ANALYZER are LC-2's and are NOT planned here - clause (e) ships a GREP, a syntax-level record for LC-2's type-aware analyzer to supersede (doc:233-235). Also out: migrating the 386 ListValue{ construction sites (LC-3), and the end-to-end AILANG repro.ail re-measurement (LC-4, doc:285-288). Planning any of these here would inflate a 2-3 day gate into a fortnight.
hard_constraints.b8_no_peak_metric: B8 reports ONLY defined before/after MemStats endpoint counters. The peak-HeapAlloc claim was REMOVED by the doc as unsupported by endpoint snapshots (doc:182-183, :420). Do not add a sampler to 'improve' it - that would enlarge a throwaway spike.
hard_constraints.external_test_package_only: ALL spike test files live in package spikelistrep_test. Clause (e) forces it for benchmarks; extending it to smoke tests keeps the package out of test-coverage-gate's denominator (P6). Do NOT add an in-package test file.

hard_constraints.commit_policy: One bisectable commit per milestone (mission standing rule). gofmt clean, go vet ./tools/... rc=0, go test -count=1 ./tools/internal/spike-listrep/... rc=0 at every milestone boundary. Commit messages carry `refs #676`, NEVER `Fixes`.

features.description: C2: chunked/unrolled cons. Nodes hold up to K elements plus a tail pointer and cached total length; elements fill leftward so a prepend into a chunk with front slack is a slot write; on front-slot contention (a second list sharing the chunk prepends) or a full chunk the prepender copies AT MOST ONE CHUNK (<= K) into a fresh node, i.e. O(K) worst case. K is a construction parameter swept at 8 and 32 - a PARAMETER STUDY of C2, not a third candidate (doc:98-100). The doc's own escape hatch applies verbatim: if the lock-free O(K) shared-chunk prepend cannot be landed in budget, C2's columns are marked INFEASIBLE with the reason recorded and the sprint proceeds, which the kill criterion tolerates if C1 passes (doc:419).
acceptance_criteria: C2 satisfies the same external-API smoke round-trip as C0/C1 at BOTH K=8 and K=32
A shared-chunk CONTENTION test exists and passes: two lists share a chunk, both prepend, both observe correct independent contents - this is the correctness claim the O(K) argument rests on
Fields unexported; all field writes inside chunklist.go's constructors
If marked infeasible: the reason is committed to README.md in this SAME commit and the C2 columns are annotated infeasible everywhere they appear
risks: Highest-uncertainty implementation in the sprint; the doc itself lists the O(K) lock-free claim as unverified (doc:419). Descope lever is doc-sanctioned, not planner-invented.

features.description: cmd/runner implementing doc:156-183 exactly. (1) Each cell in a FRESH PROCESS, FIVE TRIALS, each Go invocation with -count=1, explicit -timeout=10m, -benchmem, -benchtime=1s (the doc leaves -benchtime unpinned - plan AMB-4 pins it and records it verbatim in every cell's command), and EXACTLY ONE anchored cell regex; a 12-minute subprocess deadline kills a wedged command and the trial is REPORTED AS INVALID, never silently omitted. (2) Pairs candidate and C0 trials BY ORDINAL and computes every threshold ratio from the MEDIAN OF THE FIVE PAIRED RATIOS; clause (a)'s within-arm L-ratio and clause (d)'s within-arm n-ratio pair the two sizes by ordinal the same way. (3) Emits all raw operands, all five paired ratios, their sorted order, and the median arithmetic. (4) Applies the predeclared tie/spread rule: median exactly on a threshold, OR five ratios spanning the threshold (equality touching both sides), triggers FIVE ADDITIONAL fresh-process trials; the median of ALL TEN is final; equality passes a <= clause and passes a >= control clause. NO discretionary reruns, dropped trials, or alternate aggregation. (5) Drives B6/B8 through their main programs with the same deadlines and the same five/ten rule. (6) Records /usr/bin/time -l max RSS per invocation as NON-GATING context. Sequenced at end of Day 2 / start of Day 3 because the doc's own Timeline starts B6/B8 on Day 2 and finishes five-fresh-process runs on Day 3 (doc:358-360) - no day is added.
acceptance_criteria: Unit test: median of five paired ratios computed correctly for odd-length vectors, including unsorted input
Unit test: median EXACTLY on the threshold triggers the rerun (it is not a pass)
Unit test: five ratios SPANNING the threshold (some below, some above) triggers the rerun
Unit test: one ratio exactly equal to the threshold with the others strictly one side - equality TOUCHES BOTH sides - triggers the rerun
Unit test: after a rerun the median of ALL TEN paired ratios is used, and equality PASSES a <= clause and PASSES a >= control clause exactly as their written operators specify
Unit test: an invalid (deadline-killed) trial is surfaced as invalid and does NOT silently shrink the sample
Unit test: a cell whose regex matches != 1 benchmark is rejected before running
Runner emits, for every gated ratio, all raw operands + all five (or ten) paired ratios + sorted order + median arithmetic in machine-readable form
go vet ./tools/... rc=0; go test -count=1 ./tools/internal/spike-listrep/... rc=0
risks: The tie/spread rule has four boundary cases that are easy to get subtly wrong, on a mechanism that decides ~16 person-days. Hence the six named boundary tests are a HARD acceptance criterion, not a suggestion.
